historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly identifies the repository as an external prerequisite, but its blanket installation can select an unintended deb, conceal dependency failures and modify the host without a rollback ledger.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly treats installation and `mst start` as controlled host changes rather than a routine read-only package check.

historical_reviews.v3_1: DOCA acceptance is a reproducible package-state transition: repository identity and signature must be pinned to the exact Ubuntu release and architecture, every requested component must resolve to approved versions, dpkg must end consistent, and the tool providing `mst` plus any modules/services it starts must be explicitly recorded before comparing the DPU ID.

original_test_intent: Install the approved DOCA host software stack and supporting tools on a compatible host, then confirm the attached BlueField DPU identity through approved MST tooling.
original_method: Capture the exact host/DPU and pre-install package/service/module state, verify a pinned signed repo package and compatibility matrix, approve the full dependency set, install once with complete dpkg/apt transaction evidence, validate requested package versions and apt consistency, invoke `mst start` only under approved state-impact rules, compare every expected DPU identity, and retain a tested rollback plan.
manual_activity: The host/DPU owner approves repository/package versions, sudo and network scope, supporting-tool exceptions, `mst start` impact and the package rollback before any installation.
required_inputs: Exact host OS release and architecture
BlueField model/device ID and DPU SPEC
Pinned DOCA release and support matrix
Approved runtime/SDK/tools and Python package versions
Package providing mst and approved mst-start effects
Network or mirrored offline repository plan
Secret-safe verified SSH path if remote
safety_requirements: Do not install an unverified wildcard repo package
Do not assume internet availability or trust
Do not use password-bearing sshpass or disable host-key checks
Record complete stdout/stderr, exit statuses and apt history
Do not truncate errors with tail
Stop on dpkg/apt inconsistency or dependency removal
Do not auto-remove, downgrade, reboot or retry without approval
Treat `mst start` as a state change
Install only the approved package set
agent_execution_scope: Verify host/DPU compatibility and repo authenticity
Capture pre-install packages, repos, services and modules
Stage the exact approved package transaction
Collect complete transaction and version evidence
Verify dpkg/apt consistency and service/module changes
Run only the approved MST start/status action
Compare DPU identities and archive results without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve sudo, network/mirror and maintenance window
Decide whether sshpass is prohibited or exceptionally required
Resolve dependency, service or DPU-ID mismatch

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The command installs an unverified glob-selected repo over unauthenticated SSH, assumes internet apt, omits the source's Python dependencies, truncates apt output and never runs or validates MST/device ID. It cannot establish either complete installation or Criteria 3.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, install the exact checksum-verified repo deb and pinned package list with full dpkg/apt logs, validate versions/consistency, then run the documented approved MST initialization/status and compare all DPU IDs to the SPEC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The complete source package list, MST identity check and 15-minute estimate remain; actual transaction time follows the approved repository and dependency plan.

modernized_recommendation.status: PINNED DOCA PACKAGE TRANSACTION WITH DPU IDENTITY AND ROLLBACK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat repo installation, dependency resolution, package verification, MST initialization and DPU comparison as checkpointed stages with a pre-change snapshot and explicit rollback trigger.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes duplicate/unbounded repo steps, pins trust and versions, records all dependency/service/module effects and proves both package and DPU outcomes.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An apt zero exit or last 20 log lines cannot prove every requested component installed, no dependency was removed, MST came from the intended package or the correct DPU was detected.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repository and kernel/user-space dependency changes can destabilize networking or DPU management; rollback may require a maintenance reboot that is not automatically authorized.

project_override_considerations: Approve the DOCA/OS/BlueField compatibility tuple, repo trust chain, exact package set including Python utilities, whether `sshpass` is allowed, mst package/module behavior, expected functions/device IDs and rollback/reboot ownership.
expected_evidence: Host/OS/architecture and BlueField identity, compatibility matrix and change approval
Repo deb filename, signature/hash, source URL/mirror and pinned package versions
Pre/post repository, dpkg/apt, held/broken package, service, kernel and module manifests
Complete untruncated install transaction with exit statuses and apt history
MST package provenance, start/status output and DPU ID versus SPEC
Rollback checkpoint, preserved logs, no-blind-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, installation steps and Criteria consistently target DOCA host-stack installation followed by DPU identity verification. Duplicate repo-install wording is redundant but not a conflicting target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended package transaction and DPU verification are clear. Signed packages, compatibility, approval and rollback are identifiable prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Turns an unsafe partial apt snippet into a traceable, compatible and reversible DOCA transaction that includes every source dependency and the actual DPU-ID acceptance step.
independent_technical_reasoning: Installing a repository package changes future dependency resolution even before DOCA binaries are installed, so its trust and lifecycle are part of the test state. A correct result requires both package-graph integrity and functional DPU discovery: package success without the expected MST functions is incomplete, while a pre-existing mst binary can make DPU detection pass without proving this installation produced the approved stack.
